title: Salary Calculator: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Use our salary calculator to convert hourly to annual pay for a 38-hour week. Includes casual loading of 25% and super paid on top. Tax and fortnightly estimates for 2026-27.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week times 52 weeks, with superannuation paid on top.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for leave entitlements. Tick casual loading on the timesheet and it adds 25% to the base hourly rate you typed. Do not type a rate that already includes the loading, or the 25% is counted twice. The adult National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 an hour, and the casual floor with loading is $33.05. Remember that super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, including casual loading.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual figure from the salary calculator?
faqs.a: No, super is paid on top of your gross pay. The salary calculator shows your annual gross salary before super. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of that amount, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer would contribute an additional $7,200 in super (12% of $60,000) if you are under the cap. The calculator provides an estimate of super separately, not included in the annual gross figure.

faqs.q: How do I use the salary calculator to find my fortnightly pay?
faqs.a: Once you have your annual gross pay from the salary calculator, divide by 26 to get your gross fortnightly pay (since there are 26 fortnights in a year). For example, if your annual gross is $50,000, your gross fortnightly pay is approximately $1,923.08. The calculator also shows estimated tax and Medicare levy for the 2026-27 year, which you can subtract to estimate your net fortnightly pay. Remember that this is an estimate and does not include deductions like HELP or the Medicare levy surcharge.

bodyMarkdown:
## How the Salary Calculator Works for Australian Workers

Our **salary calculator** helps you convert an hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures based on a standard 38-hour week. The formula is straightforward: annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees, 38 hours is the standard week under the Fair Work Act. If you work part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. This applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, many workers are covered by industry or occupation awards that set higher minimum rates. For example, the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings reported by the Australian Bureau of Statistics in May 2026 were $2,083.70 per week — that is an average across all industries, not a median for any specific job. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement for your correct rate.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. So the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour. On the timesheet, type the base hourly rate and tick casual loading if it applies. The tick adds 25%. Do not type a rate that already includes the loading. The calculator then multiplies that by your weekly hours and 52 weeks to estimate annual gross pay.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation is not part of your gross salary; it is an additional contribution your employer must pay into your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. The salary calculator shows your annual gross pay and then estimates the super amount separately. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer would contribute an extra $9,600 in super (12% of $80,000) if you are under the cap. This is a key distinction: your take-home pay and your super are separate.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

To find your gross fortnightly pay, divide your annual gross by 26. For a weekly figure, divide by 52. The calculator also provides estimated tax and Medicare levy for the 2026-27 financial year using the resident tax rates: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners based on the 2025-26 single thresholds (since the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed at the time of writing). The calculator does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging arrangements.

### Using the Calculator for Different Scenarios

If you are comparing a salary offer to your current hourly rate, the salary calculator can help. For example, a full-time salary of $70,000 per year implies an hourly rate of about $35.43 (assuming 38 hours per week, 52 weeks). But remember that salary may include entitlements like paid leave, whereas an hourly rate may be casual with loading. Always consider the total package: base rate, casual loading, super, and any allowances. The calculator is a starting point; for a precise determination, consult the Fair Work Ombudsman or your employer.

For more detailed breakdowns, see [the timesheet](/) or read about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) to understand how salary sacrifice affects your figures. You can also check [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, but remember that averages are not the same as a median for your specific job.

### Important Limitations

This salary calculator provides an estimate only. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Final Thoughts

Whether you are a full-time employee, a casual worker, or comparing job offers, the salary calculator gives you a quick snapshot of your annual, fortnightly, and weekly earnings. Always verify your actual rate with your award or agreement, and remember that super is an extra benefit paid on top. Use the calculator alongside resources from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office for a complete picture.
